title: Brahmaputra River
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
info: Enters at Sadiya, leaves near Dhubri
Majuli, one of the world's largest river islands
body:
The Brahmaputra is one of Asia's great rivers. It rises in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo, flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, and then through Bangladesh, where it joins the Ganges delta.

In Assam it is wide, braided and powerful — it shapes farming, fishing and transport, and its yearly floods deposit the fertile silt the valley depends on. The river island of Majuli, in the Brahmaputra, is a centre of Assamese Vaishnavite culture.
extra:
Tributaries

Major tributaries in Assam include the Subansiri, Kameng (Jia Bharali), Manas, Sankosh, Dhansiri and Kopili from the north and south banks. The river's braided channels shift every year, creating new chars (sand islands).

Bridges

Important crossings include the Saraighat Bridge (Guwahati), the Bogibeel Bridge (Dibrugarh–Dhemaji, rail-cum-road), the Dhola–Sadiya Bridge (Bhupen Hazarika Setu, India's longest river bridge) and the Naranarayan Setu at Jogighopa.
